items.question: What kind of energy does a moving bicycle have because of its motion?
items.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of movement. Anything that moves has it: a rolling ball, a flying bird, a moving bicycle. The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

items.question: A solar panel changes light energy from the Sun into electrical energy.
items.explanation: Solar panels are made of special cells that produce electricity when sunlight falls on them. This is why they are placed on rooftops facing the Sun.

items.question: A book kept on a high shelf has energy because of its height. What is this energy called?
items.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy because of position or height. If the book falls, this stored energy turns into kinetic energy. Water stored high up in a dam works the same way.

items.question: The SI unit of energy is the ___.
items.explanation: Energy and work are both measured in joules (J). Lifting a small apple about 1 metre uses about 1 joule of energy.

items.question: A motor does 600 joules of work in 10 seconds. What is its power?
items.explanation: Power is how fast work is done: Power = Work ÷ Time. So 600 J ÷ 10 s = 60 watts (W). A 60 W bulb uses 60 joules of energy every second.
